hook: Rushing to clear $10,000 in debt might destroy your emergency fund.

sections.voiceover: Rushing to clear $10,000 in debt might destroy your emergency fund.

text_overlay.text: The Hidden Risk of Aggressive Debt Payoff

sections.voiceover: CBS News reported on October 7, 2026, that extreme payments strain household liquidity. InCharge Debt Solutions noted that cash flow suffers when balances drop too fast. Where does the emergency cash go?
b_roll: Stack of bills next to empty bank account

sections.voiceover: However, Intersect Capital planner Joe Lum warns that aggressive debt reduction creates a dangerous cash flow tightrope.
b_roll: Person walking a tightrope over city street

sections.voiceover: Freedom Debt Relief surveyed borrowers carrying at least $10,000 in non-student loans. InCharge Debt Solutions confirms that paying off debt too quickly often triggers unexpected credit score changes.
b_roll: Credit score drop notification on smartphone
Freedom Debt Relief survey report pages

sections.voiceover: Emergency cash protects you when $10,000 in debt vanishes.
